root_cause_short: Flaw in token quantity calculation logic allowed precision expansion and rounding errors to let attacker borrow or drain more than collateral justified.
exploit_steps: Attacker deployed malicious contract and took flash loan of ETH from external DEX.
Called into Radiant lending contract with crafted parameters targeting quantity/amount calculation.
Exploited rounding/precision expansion in token accounting to inflate effective borrowable amount or drain pool liquidity.
Repaid flash loan with profit extracted from protocol funds.
Funds bridged or swapped out.
invariant_broken: Token quantity and accounting calculations must conserve value exactly without exploitable rounding or precision expansion allowing excess borrow or drain.
prerequisites: Flash loan availability on source DEX
Protocol exposure to precision-sensitive quantity math in borrow/liquidation paths
mitigation_class: input sanitization and precise arithmetic libraries; bounded flash-loan impact
notes: Classic precision/rounding exploit in cross-chain lending math; X researchers highlighted similar patterns in other 2024 incidents.

root_cause_short: Loss of precision during smart contract arithmetic in Cauldrons V3/V4 allowed unauthorized MIM borrowing.
exploit_steps: Attacker funded via Tornado Cash to fresh EOAs.
Targeted specific Cauldron versions with precision-sensitive borrow logic.
Crafted transactions that triggered rounding error to borrow excess MIM against collateral.
Repeated or scaled to drain significant MIM/ETH value.
Moved funds to mixer or other addresses.
invariant_broken: Borrowed MIM amount must never exceed collateral value after all precision/rounding operations in the cauldron accounting.
prerequisites: Sufficient collateral or flash-loan capable setup
mitigation_class: use of safe math libraries with explicit precision handling; versioned contract audits
notes: Part of early 2024 precision-error wave; researchers on X noted recurring rounding issues across lending protocols.

root_cause_short: Price oracle for sUSDe manipulable via Curve; combined with aggressive rehypothecation and flash loan enabled cheap borrowing followed by liquidation or value extraction.
exploit_steps: Attacker took large flash loan (~40k-80k ETH).
Manipulated sUSDe price downward ~4% on Curve oracle used by UwU.
Borrowed heavily against undervalued collateral at depressed price.
Allowed or triggered price recovery and rehypothecation loops to extract additional value or cause protocol loss.
Repaid flash loan; extracted ~$19M+ profit.
Funds laundered via mixers.
invariant_broken: Oracle price used for borrowing/liquidation must reflect true market value without single-pool manipulation; collateral health must account for rehypothecation risk.
prerequisites: Oracle dependency on manipulable Curve pool for sUSDe
mitigation_class: oracle diversity and TWAP; borrow caps; reduced rehypothecation multipliers
notes: Rich X forensics from SlowMist and on-chain trackers showed clear flash-loan + oracle path; one of clearest 2024 oracle+flashloan cases.

root_cause_short: Closed-source router exposed arbitrary-call capability via insufficient validation of user-supplied inputs, allowing abuse of existing unlimited token approvals to invoke transferFrom.
exploit_steps: Attacker monitored or knew of users with unlimited approvals to SwapNet/Matcha-integrated contracts.
Called vulnerable arbitrary-call function on SwapNet router with crafted parameters.
Function forwarded call to execute transferFrom on user-approved ERC20 tokens.
Drained tokens directly from user wallets to attacker-controlled addresses across Ethereum, Arbitrum, Base, BSC.
Swapped stolen assets (e.g. large USDC to ETH on Base) and bridged.
Funds partially mixed.
invariant_broken: User token approvals granted to the protocol may only be exercised for protocol-intended swap/liquidity operations; no arbitrary third-party contract can trigger transferFrom on behalf of users via the router.
prerequisites: Users had granted unlimited approvals to SwapNet or integrated aggregator
Vulnerable arbitrary-call path in closed-source contract
mitigation_class: revoke unlimited approvals; strict input validation and whitelisting of callable functions; approval scoping
notes: PeckShield and BlockSec provided rapid on-chain + decompile analysis. Some researchers noted it as the largest approval-drain attack outside pure phishing. Matcha users primarily impacted; urgent revoke calls on X.

root_cause_short: V3/V4 contracts had arbitrary-call vulnerability from insufficient input validation, enabling abuse of existing ERC20/NFT approvals to drain via transferFrom.
exploit_steps: Attacker targeted specific vulnerable versions of Aperture V3/V4 contracts.
Invoked arbitrary-call path with malicious parameters.
Executed transferFrom on user-approved tokens and liquidity position NFTs.
Drained ~$3.67M across Ethereum, Arbitrum, Base.
Attacker addresses later deposited significant ETH into Tornado Cash.
Protocol paused front-end and advised approval reviews.
invariant_broken: Approved tokens and NFTs held or managed by the protocol can only be moved via intended protocol functions; arbitrary calls cannot trigger unauthorized transferFrom.
prerequisites: Users/positions with approvals to vulnerable Aperture contract versions
mitigation_class: strict calldata validation and function whitelisting; scoped approvals; immediate pause on anomaly
notes: BlockSec linked the vulnerability pattern to SwapNet incident (same day). Some on-chain analysis (PeckShield) treated the two as concurrent but technically unrelated exploits by possibly different actors using same bug class. Funds traced to Tornado Cash.

root_cause_short: Attacker compromised contractor GitHub credentials, pivoted to AWS KMS, and exfiltrated SERVICE_ROLE private key used for protocol operations.
exploit_steps: Social engineering or credential theft targeted contractor GitHub account.
Used access to infiltrate AWS environment and KMS.
Extracted SERVICE_ROLE private key controlling critical protocol functions or funds.
Used key to drain or move protocol assets (~$24.5M).
Rapid exfiltration and laundering.
invariant_broken: Critical operational keys (KMS SERVICE_ROLE etc.) must be protected by hardware-backed, multi-party, or least-privilege controls with no single contractor credential path.
prerequisites: Contractor with GitHub access to repo tied to AWS
Long-lived high-privilege KMS keys without rotation or HSM enforcement
mitigation_class: hardware security modules; short-lived credentials; GitHub SSO + 2FA + audit logging; key rotation policies
notes: Classic supply-chain-to-KMS path; X community and infra researchers emphasized contractor access hygiene. No public detailed post-mortem contradicting initial reports.

root_cause_short: DPRK-linked actors used 6-month social engineering campaign to obtain pre-signed transactions from Security Council members via durable nonces, then introduced fake collateral token with manipulated oracle price to drain vaults.
exploit_steps: Long-term social engineering compromised or tricked Drift contributors/signers (UNC4736 / Citrine Sleet / Lazarus tradecraft).
Used Solana durable nonces to obtain pre-signed admin transactions from council members.
Submitted pre-signed tx to transfer admin control to attacker address.
Removed withdrawal limits and vault permissions.
Deployed/introduced worthless fake token (e.g. CarbonVote-like), manipulated its price via wash trading and fake liquidity on Raydium to create artificial oracle value.
Listed fake token as collateral and rapidly withdrew real assets (USDC, SOL, JLP, WBTC etc.) worth ~$285M in ~12 minutes.
Laundered via mixers and bridges.
invariant_broken: Only assets with genuine, manipulation-resistant oracles and verified collateral status may be used for borrowing or withdrawal; admin and signer actions must not be bypassable via social engineering or pre-signed nonce abuse.
prerequisites: Ability to quickly create and oracle-manipulate fake collateral asset
mitigation_class: hardware signing with policy enforcement; no durable nonce for high-privilege actions; oracle circuit breakers and collateral listing timelocks; multi-party computation or stricter council processes
notes: Extensive X and on-chain forensics by Elliptic, TRM Labs, Chainalysis attributed to DPRK with high confidence. Social engineering + durable nonces + fake collateral oracle manip was novel combination. One of the largest Solana DeFi losses.

root_cause_short: Misconfigured or stale oracle parameters allowed incorrect price feeds leading to improper liquidations or value extraction.
exploit_steps: Attacker monitored oracle configuration on Silo markets.
Exploited misconfig to borrow or liquidate at distorted prices.
Extracted small but notable value before correction.
Protocol or community responded with config fix.
invariant_broken: Oracle prices used for borrowing, collateral valuation, and liquidation must be fresh, correctly sourced, and match intended market parameters at all times.
prerequisites: Oracle config error or stale feed exposure in specific market
mitigation_class: oracle health checks; automated circuit breakers; conservative config defaults
notes: Smaller April 2026 incident; part of broader month with high incident count. X researchers noted recurring oracle config issues across lending protocols.

root_cause_short: KelpDAO used 1-of-1 DVN configuration for LayerZero OFT bridge; attacker forged cross-chain message by targeting off-chain verifier infrastructure (compromised or forced via DDoS/RPC), bypassing multi-verifier security to mint/unlock unbacked rsETH.
exploit_steps: Attacker (linked to Lazarus) identified KelpDAO rsETH LayerZero OFT adapter with single-DVN (LayerZero Labs only) setup.
Forged or spoofed cross-chain message/packet claiming origin from another chain (e.g. Unichain).
Exploited sole-verifier path (possibly via RPC compromise or DDoS forcing fallback) to have message accepted on destination.
Unlocked/minted ~116,500 unbacked rsETH on Ethereum escrow.
Drained ~$292M value rapidly.
Laundered funds; LayerZero subsequently deprecated 1-of-1 configs.
invariant_broken: Cross-chain messages for bridge/OFT must be verified by diverse, independent DVNs; no single verifier or off-chain component may unilaterally authorize mint/unlock of tokens.
prerequisites: Ability to forge or force acceptance of spoofed message via verifier/RPC path
mitigation_class: mandatory multi-DVN diversity; on-chain message validation redundancy; monitoring of verifier health and config
notes: Largest single DeFi exploit of 2026 to date. X and on-chain analysis (Chainalysis, Galaxy, LayerZero team) quickly identified the 1-of-1 DVN as root cause. Attributed to DPRK Lazarus with preliminary confidence. Highlighted systemic bridge config risk.
